summary: Boise NF lookout site first set up in 1908 as Bald Mtn.; current L-4 cab built 1933, staffed as needed and available for emergencies; registered 2020.

access.note: Sources describe it as staffed as needed and available for emergencies. None describes public entry into the cab.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as drive-up. The sources give no trail or road route; check with the Boise National Forest before going.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest

events.note: Lookout site named Bald Mtn. established; first structure a wooden ground-mounted cab (firelookout.com only).
Current structure: L-4 cab on a tower base. NHLR and firelookout.com give a 10-foot base; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives an 8-foot log crib.
L-4 modified and set on a concrete basement, in the 1960s (decade only; no exact year given).
Linda Bellmer Bass listed as relief staff, 1974-1982, per a former fire lookout registry book (as cited by Idaho Fire Lookouts). Earliest staffing given in the sources.
End of the listed relief-staff period (Idaho Fire Lookouts). Not a documented end of all staffing.
Set to emergency service, in the 2000s (decade only; no exact year given).
Registered September 28, 2020 as NHLR US 1431, ID 123.

evidence.supports: site set up 1908 as Bald Mtn. with wooden ground-mounted first cab
evidence.quote: Established in 1908 a lookout site named Bald Mtn., the first structure was a wooden ground-mounted cab.
Thorn Creek Butte was constructed in 1933.

evidence.supports: classic L-4 cabin atop a 10-foot enclosed tower
evidence.quote: A classic L-4 cabin atop a 10 foot enclosed tower.

evidence.supports: 1933 L-4 cab on an 8-foot log crib (Idaho Fire Lookouts)
10-foot base topped with L-4 cab in 1933 (firelookout.com)
evidence.quote: In 1933, the present 10' base topped with an L-4 cab was constructed.

evidence.supports: 1933 two-story structure with L-4 cab (Forest Lookouts)
evidence.quote: 1933: A two-story lookout structure with a L-4 cab constructed.

evidence.supports: Linda Bellmer Bass cited from former fire lookout registry book
evidence.quote: Linda Bellmer Bass (Former Fire Lookout Registry Book) — Relief
The lookout is available for emergencies.
US Forest Service - Boise National Forest

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts page all give 1933 for the current L-4 cab. The 1908 Bald Mtn. date and wooden first cab come only from firelookout.com and refer to an earlier structure on the same site.
NHLR and firelookout.com say 10 feet; Idaho Fire Lookouts gives an 8-foot log crib for 1933 and later a concrete basement. The story reports both figures.

NHLR says available for emergencies; firelookout.com says staffed as needed; Idaho Fire Lookouts says drive-up staffed-as-needed and set to emergency service in the 2000s. Read as staffed as needed, with emergency use.

sources.title: Thorn Creek Butte Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Current status is not confirmed. A search result titled 'Thorn Creek Butte Lookout Tower [CLOSED]' on AllTrails could not be opened (HTTP 403), so it is not relied on; verify before any visit. No Forest Service page for this lookout was found. Not on the FFLA rentals list as far as the grep showed. The 1974-1982 staffing dates are the only dated staffing. The brief's access 'unknown' is now 'restricted' on the basis of the sources' emergency-only language, which is a judgement call. A 2026 Crooked Fire closure near Idaho City appeared in search results but was not checked against this site.
